report.clinical_summary: Patient presents with fatigue, night sweats, and swollen neck that have been worsening over several months. Work capacity has been substantially reduced - can no longer work full days, needs breaks and naps, and has given up hobbies and social activities. Patient has been diagnosed with CLL and is currently on active surveillance with regular blood tests. They are actively trying to manage stress, get more rest, maintain healthy lifestyle, and seek support from family/friends. Trusts medical team and believes treatment will be effective if needed.

evidence.quote: I used to be able to work a full day without any problem, but now even getting through the morning is a struggle
Lately, I've been having to take more breaks than usual and sometimes even nap during lunchtime just to get some energy back
As for hobbies or leisure activities, I find myself feeling too tired to do anything enjoyable after coming home from work. Even watching TV or reading a book is often too exhausting
It's been really difficult to maintain my usual social life as well since meeting up with friends usually involves staying out late, which is just not feasible anymore
Overall, the symptoms have really taken a toll on my energy level and quality of life

consequences.reasoning: Patient has had to significantly reduce work capacity (can't get through mornings, needs breaks and naps), given up hobbies (too tired for TV, reading), and can't maintain social life. This is a major role reduction - work is substantially reduced.

evidence.quote: I definitely see my condition as a slow-moving disease, so I expect things to continue at their current pace
The fact that my symptoms have been worsening over the past few months is concerning, but if treatment does end up being necessary, I trust it will be done in a timely and effective manner

timeline.reasoning: Patient explicitly states they see it as a slow-moving disease and expect things to continue at current pace. They acknowledge worsening symptoms but don't expect sudden changes.

evidence.quote: I feel like my hands are somewhat tied since there doesn't seem to be any particular trigger or lifestyle choice that might have caused these symptoms in the first place
However, I am trying to make some changes to better manage stress levels at work and maybe find ways to get more rest throughout the day

I've also been thinking about reaching out to friends and family for support — not just for emotional reasons but also because they might be able to help me with errands or tasks that would otherwise exhaust me
Overall, I feel like there's only so much I can do until we have a better grasp on what we're dealing with here
I'm focused on doing everything in my power to maintain a healthy lifestyle — eating well, staying active, and continuing to prioritize self-care as much as possible
